audit_findings.title: The anchor does not reflect the full interest burden of the post-buyback capital structure
audit_findings.magnitude: 2026 first-half interest expense was $140.1 million versus $92.7 million in 2025, a $47.4 million increase; the $280.2 million annualized 2026 amount is $70.311 million above FY2025 interest expense of $209.889 million, before tax
audit_findings.mechanism: The equity-level OE anchor retains interest expense, so the FY2025 anchor combines partial-year interest with the later, reduced share count and June 2026 capital structure.
audit_findings.evidence: On August 8, 2025, we issued $1.25 billion aggregate principal amount of 5.25% Senior Unsecured Notes due 2035 (the “2035 Senior Notes”) in a registered public offering.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated timing mismatch. The computed pre-tax gap is 5.4% of the $1,303.5 million anchor and would recur throughout the forecast, making it reasonably capable of materially changing the intrinsic-value estimates even though the exact after-tax OE adjustment is not established.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile FY2025 interest by debt instrument, replace partial-year amounts with the June 2026 principal-and-rate run rate, determine the recurring after-tax OE reduction, and rerun every scenario without changing the stated growth or discount-rate inputs.

audit_findings.title: The bridge appears to add operating cash as though it were surplus cash
audit_findings.magnitude: $225.0-$275.0 million, or $3.01-$3.68 per diluted share; 0.92%-1.12% of the $24,467 million base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds all $356.4 million of cash even though $225.0-$275.0 million is identified as the operating minimum; only $81.4-$131.4 million is presumptively excess before other restrictions.
audit_findings.evidence: We typically seek to maintain minimum cash balances globally of approximately $225.0 million to $275.0 million for general operating purposes.
audit_findings.explanation: Adding required operating cash is a demonstrated bridge error. Removing the filed operating minimum would reduce base value from $327.46 to approximately $323.78-$324.45 per share, which is too small to alter the valuation conclusion relative to the $573.01 market price.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the precise operating minimum and any restricted or near-term committed cash, then replace the $356.4 million bridge addition with verified excess cash.

audit_findings.title: Historical growth may include acquisitions whose purchase cost is absent from OE
audit_findings.magnitude: $696.8 million filed cash purchase price for the remaining Burgiss interest; valuation effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Acquired earnings can increase the historical OE growth used to support the 8%-10% scenarios, while acquisition payments remain outside recurring OE and the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: On October 2, 2023, the Company acquired the remaining 66.4 % interest in The Burgiss Group, LLC (“Burgiss”) for $ 696.8 million in cash.
audit_findings.explanation: The acquisition and its cash cost are demonstrated, but the record does not separate acquired from organic OE growth or establish how much acquisition spending would be required to sustain the forecast. The possible distortion affects the growth assumption over the full DCF and could be material, but its magnitude cannot be established from the supplied schedule.
audit_findings.action: Prepare an acquisition-by-acquisition bridge separating organic revenue, operating profit and OE growth from acquired contributions and purchase payments; then rerun the valuation using a growth path demonstrably fundable by retained OE.

audit_findings.title: A concentrated, market-linked fee stream may not support smooth growth
audit_findings.magnitude: BlackRock represented a computed $338.5 million of FY2025 revenue and $202.7 million of first-half 2026 revenue; approximately $326.7 million and $195.8 million, respectively, were market-linked under the filed percentages
audit_findings.mechanism: Changes in market levels, flows and fee rates affect OE growth through asset-based revenue rather than through stable subscription growth alone.
audit_findings.evidence: For the year ended December 31, 2025, our largest client organization by revenue, BlackRock, accounted for 10.8% of our consolidated operating revenues, with 96.5% of the operating revenues from BlackRock coming from fees based on the assets in BlackRock’s ETFs and non-ETF products that are based on our indexes .
audit_findings.explanation: The concentration and market linkage are demonstrated, but no present misstatement or adverse fee change is established. BlackRock concentration rose from 10.8% in FY2025 to 11.8% in first-half 2026 while asset-based revenue was growing, so the exposure can move value in either direction and is presently a scenario risk to monitor.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the effective economics of the January 2026 amendment, track BlackRock revenue, indexed AUM, flows and realized basis-point fees quarterly, and stress those drivers if fee compression, outflows or adverse amendment effects appear.

audit_findings.title: The latest-actual anchor retains a material nonrecurring tax charge
audit_findings.magnitude: $38 million, equal to 2.9% of anchor OE; if fully retained, removing it would add approximately $9.41 per share to base value and $6.59 to the buy-below price
audit_findings.mechanism: A nonrecurring tax expense reduces FY2025 net income and therefore OE if it was not separately normalized; the separate $88 million 2026 benefit must likewise be excluded from recurring OE.
audit_findings.evidence: The increase in the effective tax rate in 2025 was driven by $38 million of expense recognized in connection with a multi-phase internal legal entity restructuring that commenced in the period and was completed subsequent to year end.
audit_findings.explanation: The $38 million charge and $88 million benefit are filed facts, although the summarized OE schedule does not independently prove whether the charge was already adjusted. Even assuming the entire charge remains in OE, the computed base value would rise only from $327.46 to about $336.87 per share and would remain far below the $573.01 market price, so it cannot change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Trace both restructuring tax entries through the OE workpaper, add back the $38 million only if it remains in FY2025 OE, exclude the $88 million benefit from normalized earnings, and document the recurring cash-tax rate.

audit_findings.title: Contingent acquisition consideration may be an unbridged claim ahead of common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: $33.9 million at June 30, 2026, or approximately $0.45 per diluted share and 0.14% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Contingent acquisition consideration is paid through financing cash flow and can therefore escape OE while remaining a contractual claim that should reduce the equity bridge unless already captured elsewhere.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, the fair value of the contingent consideration was $ 14.6 million, of which $ 9.6 million is included in “Other accrued liabilities” and $ 5.0 million is included in “Other non-current liabilities” on the Consolidated Statement of Financial Condition.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest filing establishes a $33.9 million liability, increased from $14.6 million at year-end after new acquisitions. If the full latest balance is omitted, deducting it would reduce base value from $327.46 to approximately $327.01 per share, which is not material to the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the June 2026 $33.9 million liability to the OE schedule and bridge, deduct any uncaptured amount from equity value, and update the balance for subsequent payments or fair-value changes.
